paper_title: Constraints on light decaying dark matter candidates from 16 years of INTEGRAL/SPI observations
notes: Paper sets new 95% CL upper limits on decaying DM from 16 yr of INTEGRAL/SPI data. Primary ALP result is Fig. 3 (g_agamma vs m_a, 60 keV - 16 MeV), derived from the 2-gamma decay-rate limits in Fig. 1 via Eq. 6: Gamma_2gamma = 0.755e-30 (g/1e-20 GeV^-1)^2 (m/100 keV)^3 s^-1. No numerical table is provided; the data_points above are approximate values reconstructed from the figures assuming the benchmark 1D global-fit limit (Gamma_2gamma ~ 1e-28 s^-1 scale) converted through Eq. 6, so they should be treated as digitization-level estimates. The Fig. 1 limit is 'noisy' bin-to-bin, so individual points may deviate by factors of a few. Analysis assumes NFW halo profile (Karukes et al. 2020) with D-factor 1.289e29 keV/cm^2 over |l|,|b|<47.5 deg — a Galactic halo decay bound, not a local-density haloscope, so dm_density_assumed is null.
